findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds and mutates a config copy (converting schedule_type to its display value) but then returns the raw monitor.config in the dict, so the schedule_type display conversion is dead code and the serialized context carries the raw enum value. Consumers of the monitor issue context (UI/event payload) receive e.g. schedule_type: 'crontab' instead of the human display value the surrounding code clearly intends; anyone debugging incident payloads sees the code value and the copied config is silently discarded.

[ADVISORY] The public module surface of mark_failed loses mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, and SimpleCheckIn with no compatibility re-export, while the diff contains no updates to any importer of those symbols. Any in-tree or out-of-tree code (including existing tests that patch/assert against mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence or mark_failed.get_failure_reason) fails with ImportError/AttributeError at import or patch time; moved-but-unreferenced helpers have no verified caller census in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The threshold query filters only on date_added__lte with no status bound and no tie-break on id, so the 'consecutive failures' window is computed against all check-ins including OK check-ins arriving with equal timestamps, and ordering among same-timestamp check-ins is nondeterministic. With check-ins sharing a timestamp (batched/clock-skewed submissions), reversed() over an unordered slice can include an OK check-in in or exclude a failed one from the threshold window, producing a missed incident or a premature incident; behavior is carried verbatim from the old code but now lives in a new module with no test in this diff exercising the equal-timestamp or mixed-status ordering path.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds a modified copy of monitor.config (humanizing schedule_type) but then returns the raw unmodified monitor.config, so the schedule_type humanization is dead code and the raw enum/int value ships to the event context. Consumers of the monitor context in the issue event see the raw schedule_type value instead of the intended display name; anyone changing this function later has two sources of config to reason about. This defect was carried verbatim from mark_failed.py during the move rather than fixed or flagged.

[ADVISORY] The module split leaves the incident-creation entry point named try_incident_threshold in incidents.py while occurrence creation lives in incident_occurrence.py, but mark_failed.py still orchestrates both, so the 'reorganize' adds an indirection layer without a single-source entry point for incident lifecycle. Future callers must know to call mark_failed (which does pre-processing then delegates) rather than the logic modules directly; the next change to incident flow (e.g. marking resolved) has to reverse-engineer which module owns which responsibility.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes and mutates a local `config` copy (converting schedule_type to its display value) but then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` unchanged, so the humanized schedule_type never reaches the occurrence context. Every monitor incident occurrence's `contexts.monitor.config` ships the raw stored config (e.g. schedule_type as 'crontab'/'interval' enum value) instead of the display label the dead code was written to produce; the mutation is silently discarded on every call.

[ADVISORY] The occurrence loop fetches full MonitorCheckIn rows via filter(id__in=...) without select_related('monitor_environment'), then create_incident_occurrence accesses failed_checkin.monitor_environment, issuing one additional query per check-in (N+1). For failure_issue_threshold > 1, the incident-creation path issues 1 query for the check-ins plus N queries for monitor_environment (plus get_last_successful_checkin and get_environment per occurrence), multiplying DB load exactly when a monitor is failing repeatedly; carried over verbatim from mark_failed.py in this move.

[ADVISORY] When failure_issue_threshold > 1 and the threshold is met, the loop creates one Kafka occurrence per failed check-in (N occurrences for a single incident), each citing the same full failed_checkins list — the loop's per-checkin parameterization is indistinguishable in output from a single occurrence, suggesting the loop is redundant. Downstream issue-platform consumers receive up to failure_issue_threshold duplicate IssueOccurrences with distinct event_ids for one incident transition, potentially creating duplicate events on the same fingerprint; if intentional this needs a comment, if not it is an amplification bug carried into the new module.

[ADVISORY] The status transition to MonitorStatus.ERROR is a read-modify-write (status checked in Python, then save(update_fields=('status',)) with no WHERE status IN (...) guard), so two concurrent failed check-ins can both pass the OK/ACTIVE check and both execute the incident-creation branch. Under concurrent check-in processing for the same monitor environment, duplicate incident transitions and duplicate occurrences can be produced; get_or_create on MonitorIncident partially contains the damage but the double occurrence production and double signal dispatch are not idempotent. Carried over from mark_failed.py by this move, so not a regression, but the refactor is the natural place to note it.

[ADVISORY] create_incident_occurrence silently returns without producing an occurrence when monitor_env is None, conflating 'no environment' with success at a call site where try_incident_threshold has already guaranteed monitor_env is not None. The failed_checkin parameter's monitor_environment can never be None on any current call path (try_incident_threshold returns False earlier for a None env), so this dead branch masks a would-be invariant violation instead of surfacing it; if a future caller passes an orphaned check-in, occurrences are silently dropped with no log. Carried over from the moved code.

[ADVISORY] get_monitor_environment_context builds and mutates a local `config` (translating schedule_type to its display value) but then returns the original unmodified `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, making the computed copy dead code. The monitor context shipped in event_data carries the raw `schedule_type` value (e.g. crontab int/str) rather than the human-readable display value the local mutation clearly intends; future contributors editing the function will reasonably assume the mutated config is what is sent and 'fix' behavior unintentionally.

[ADVISORY] get_failure_reason has an inconsistent return type: the singular path returns a lazy `_StrPromise` while the plural path returns an eagerly-formatted str, so callers must remember to wrap in str(). Any future caller that uses the return value directly (e.g. storing it in evidence_data or logging) will emit a lazy-proxy object instead of a string; the current caller only survives because it happens to call str() around the value.

[BUG] get_monitor_environment_context computes a translated config copy (config["schedule_type"] = get_schedule_type_display()) but then returns the raw monitor.config in the payload, discarding the translation entirely. Every monitor incident occurrence embeds the raw numeric/internal schedule_type value in event_data.contexts.monitor.config instead of the human-readable display value, so consumers of the occurrence payload (issue UI/serialization) receive the untranslated enum value; the copied-and-mutated `config` variable is dead code, signalling the author intended the display value but the payload never uses it.

[ADVISORY] In the MonitorStatus.ERROR branch, monitor_env.active_incident can be None, in which case the occurrence creation is silently skipped by `if ... and incident:` yet the function still returns True and fires monitor_environment_failed with no log. When an environment is in ERROR status but has no resolvable active incident (e.g. get_or_create raced or the incident row was resolved concurrently), the failure is reported as handled and the signal fires, but no issue occurrence is ever produced and nothing is logged — the dropped work is invisible to operators debugging a missing monitor-failure issue.

[ADVISORY] monitor_env.status is persisted as ERROR and the MonitorIncident row is committed before create_incident_occurrence runs, and a failure inside create_incident_occurrence/produce_occurrence_to_kafka leaves the incident state committed with no issue created, no rollback, and no compensating log. If the Kafka produce path raises (serialization error, broker unavailable), mark_failed has already returned-failed semantics to callers via the exception mid-function after the DB commit: the monitor environment is permanently marked ERROR with an incident row but the corresponding Sentry issue never exists, and the next failed check-in takes the ERROR branch producing an occurrence for a user who never saw the original threshold-crossing issue — the state transition is not atomic with the notification work it claims to have performed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, `get_monitor_environment_context`, and the local `SimpleCheckIn` from `src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py`, moving related logic into new modules (`incident_occurrence.py`, `incidents.py`, and `monitors/types.py`) and only leaving `mark_failed()` to call `try_incident_threshold()`. There is no compatibility re-export in `mark_failed.py` (e.g., `from ... import get_failure_reason as get_failure_reason`), so any existing code that imports/patches these symbols from `mark_failed` would break. However, the diff does not show any actual import sites or failing tests, so the breakage is a grounded risk/compatibility concern rather than a diff-provable defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the threshold window is built via `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(monitor_environment=monitor_env, date_added__lte=failed_checkin.date_added).order_by("-date_added").values(...)` and then sliced/reversed. Because ordering is only by `date_added` with no secondary key (e.g. `-id`), rows with identical `date_added` have nondeterministic order, so the chosen `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` can vary. That can incorrectly include/exclude an OK check-in in the window (the code explicitly returns False if any OK is present), changing whether an incident is triggered. This behavior exists in the diff as moved logic (it was previously in `mark_failed_threshold`), and the diff adds no test coverage for the equal-timestamp ordering edge case.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `incidents.py`), the code loads check-ins with `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...])` and then calls `create_incident_occurrence(previous_checkins, checkin, ...)` for each result. Inside `create_incident_occurrence` (new `incident_occurrence.py`), it immediately accesses `failed_checkin.monitor_environment` and then calls `monitor_env.get_last_successful_checkin()` and `monitor_env.get_environment().name`. The queryset in `try_incident_threshold` does not use `select_related('monitor_environment')` (or prefetch of environment/monitor), so each `checkin.monitor_environment` access can trigger an extra query per row (N+1), with additional queries potentially coming from the helper calls. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), when an incident is active and not muted it does `checkins = MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[c["id"] for c in previous_checkins])` and then loops `for checkin in checkins: create_incident_occurrence(previous_checkins, checkin, ...)`. `create_incident_occurrence` uses the full `failed_checkins` list for the evidence (`get_failure_reason(failed_checkins)`) and otherwise produces a new `IssueOccurrence` with a fresh `event_id` each time, so this can emit up to `failure_issue_threshold` occurrences for one incident transition. The diff shows this duplication behavior clearly, but it’s not definitively a defect from the diff alone (it could be intentional, e.g. per-checkin trace_id differences), so the actionable review point is to clarify intent or consolidate to a single occurrence if duplicates are not desired.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the code checks `monitor_env.status in [MonitorStatus.OK, MonitorStatus.ACTIVE]` in Python and then performs `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` followed by `monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",))` without an atomic/conditional DB update (no `WHERE status IN (...)`). Under concurrent processing for the same `monitor_env`, two workers can both enter this branch, both attempt the transition, and both proceed to create/send occurrences and dispatch `monitor_environment_failed`. While `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)` reduces duplicate incident rows, it does not prevent duplicate occurrence production and signal dispatch shown in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_incident_occurrence`, the function fetches `monitor_env = failed_checkin.monitor_environment` and immediately `return`s if it is `None` (new file `incident_occurrence.py`). In the only shown call path (`try_incident_threshold` in `incidents.py`), `monitor_env` is checked for `None` at the top and returns `False` early, and the `previous_checkins` IDs are sourced from `failed_checkin` or from a queryset filtered by `monitor_environment=monitor_env`, so the subsequent `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=...)` should yield checkins with a non-null environment on this path. Thus, the branch is likely redundant/dead for current call paths, and the silent return could hide an invariant violation if a future caller passes an orphaned check-in. This is a maintainability/robustness concern rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `incident_occurrence.py`, `get_failure_reason` returns `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP[...]` on the singular path, which is a lazy translation proxy (`_StrPromise`). On the plural path it returns `_('...') % {...}`, and Django’s lazy proxy `%` formatting typically forces `str(...)` and yields an actual `str`. So the return type is inconsistent across branches. The current call site wraps it in `str(...)` (`value=str(get_failure_reason(...))`), but a future caller that doesn’t could end up propagating a lazy proxy instead of a concrete string.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` the DB state transition is persisted before producing the occurrence: `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` then `monitor_env.save(...)` and `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)` happen before calling `create_incident_occurrence(...)` (which calls `produce_occurrence_to_kafka(...)`) with no surrounding transaction or exception handling. Under Django autocommit, if Kafka production raises, the function will exit via exception after the DB writes are committed, leaving the monitor env in ERROR and an incident row created without the corresponding occurrence/issue notification work completing, matching the described non-atomic behavior.
